blocks.text: Condo buildings in Cultus Lake
Cultus Lake East is FVRD Electoral Area H plus Cultus Lake Park Board lease land — it is not inside the City of Chilliwack, whatever mailing addresses say.

The north end of Cultus Lake is FVRD Electoral Area H plus Cultus Lake Park, governed by the Cultus Lake Park Board — it is not inside the City of Chilliwack, whatever mailing addresses say. Lakeside at Cultus Lake is filed in full HERE.

The south end of Cultus Lake, including Lindell Beach on the south shore, is FVRD Electoral Area H — outside the Cultus Lake Park Board lease lands and not inside the City of Chilliwack, whatever mailing addresses say. The three Lindell Beach communities (Creekside Mills, The Cottages at Cultus Lake, Aquadel Crossing) are filed in full HERE, classified by their actual sourced tenure — all three are bare-land strata single-family/cottage communities, not apartment condos.
Lakeside at Cultus Lake — 3175 Columbia Valley Highway (north end)

A waterfront condominium building of 21 homes, developed by Alture Properties with Jim Young on freehold waterfront land (developer source); the developer calls it "a collection of 21 condominium homes" just inside the boundary of the provincial park, each home with a private deck, a boat slip and two parking stalls. Listing data records the building as Apartment/Condo type, built 2019, in board Area Minor "Cultus Lake North"; the building's own site states only 5 of its 21 homes remain, with a private dock and a boat slip for each home. Tenure/form for condo purposes, verified fresh: a freehold strata-form condominium building — not Park Board leasehold, not bare-land strata, not a pad product.
Where the condos are and what to know

items.t: No official boundary for Cultus Lake East is published by the Cultus Lake Park Board, the FVRD or BC Parks. The Cultus Lake Park Plan, Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, designates the residential lots on the east side of the lake and the Mountainview Road and Park Drive areas as Residential, and BC Parks states Columbia Valley Highway bisects the southeast section of Cultus Lake Provincial Park.

Where condo stock concentrates: it does not exist on the east shore. Most of the east shore is Cultus Lake Provincial Park (Entrance Bay, Clear Creek, Delta Grove and Maple Bay campgrounds; Entrance Bay and Maple Bay day-use areas); the private housing is the Park lease-lot strip on Lakeshore Drive and Munroe Avenue (R-3 Waterfront Residential and R-4 Hillside Residential zones in FVRD Cultus Lake Park Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016) plus one manufactured-home park on Columbia Valley Highway.
Tenure (the defining fact): east-side homes inside Cultus Lake Park are on leased lots under the Cultus Lake Park Board — leasehold, not freehold.
Area-level feeder pattern only (SD33 Administrative Procedure 611): Cultus Lake Elementary School → Mount Slesse Middle School → G.W.

Transit and shopping: BC Transit route 56 Cultus Lake runs along Columbia Valley Highway on the east-shore side, seasonal — summer only, with no year-round service. No shopping centre or grocery store on the east shore is confirmed.

No official MLS boundary for Cultus Lake North is published by the Park Board or the FVRD. The Park Board states Cultus Lake Park covers 640 acres at the north end of the lake, with the Village Centre site immediately south of Columbia Valley Highway at Sunnyside Boulevard. "Cultus Lake North" is used by the FVRD as a community location name in its Area H Evacuation Guide; it is not a municipal neighbourhood name.

Where condo stock concentrates: in exactly one building. The north end's housing is otherwise single-detached homes and cabins on Park Board leased lots along Sunnyside Boulevard and the Park's residential streets; the one condominium, Lakeside at Cultus Lake, stands at 3175 Columbia Valley Highway at the lake's north end, on freehold waterfront land outside the Park lease system (developer source). Townhome complexes in Cultus Lake North: none confirmed.

Tenure (the defining contrast inside one sub-area): homes inside Cultus Lake Park sit on leased lots administered by the Cultus Lake Park Board under the Cultus Lake Park Act — leasehold, not freehold. Lakeside is the exception: the developer describes freehold waterfront land.
Graham Secondary), and G.W. Graham Secondary.

Village, transit and shopping: Main Beach is the Park Board's main public beach at the north end; Sunnyside Campground, 4165 Columbia Valley Highway, is 65 acres with seasonal, full hook-up and tenting sites, a boat launch and playgrounds; Cultus Lake Community Hall is at 4220 Columbia Valley Highway. The Village Centre / plaza at Columbia Valley Highway and Sunnyside Boulevard is the Park commercial area designated in PlanCultus, and a Park Board committee agenda names Cultus Lake Superette as its grocery and convenience store. BC Transit route 56 runs between Chilliwack (Cottonwood Mall / Promontory area) and the Cultus Lake Marina stop via Vedder Road and Columbia Valley Highway — seasonal, summer months only, no year-round service.

No official MLS boundary for Cultus Lake South is published by the FVRD or the Park Board. The FVRD lists Lindell Beach, Columbia Valley and Cultus Lake as the communities of Electoral Area H, and also uses "Cultus Lake South" as a community name — it publishes a Cultus Lake South Community Emergency Preparedness Guide.

Where condo stock concentrates: there is no apartment-condo stock at the south end. The attached/stratified stock clusters along Columbia Valley Road at Lindell Beach as bare-land strata single-family communities: Creekside Mills (1687 Columbia Valley Rd, developer source), The Cottages at Cultus Lake (1777 Columbia Valley Rd) and Aquadel Crossing (1885 Columbia Valley Rd, developer source), with the Lindell Beach Holiday Resort at 1920 Columbia Valley Rd. Columbia Valley Road provides one-way-in, one-way-out access, north to the Sardis and Yarrow exits of Highway 1.

Tenure (the defining contrast): unlike the north and east shores, south-end homes are outside the Cultus Lake Park leasehold system — tenure here is freehold lots plus bare land strata, under the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115; PlanCultus (Bylaw No. 1080, 2016) applies only inside Cultus Lake Park at the north end. Under the OCP designations the only residential use permitted is single family residential use, with housing needs met mainly through infill in existing hamlets.

Transit, shopping and services: BC Transit route 56 ends at the Cultus Lake Marina stop at the north end and does not extend to Lindell Beach; service to the lake is seasonal, summer only. No shopping centre or grocery store at the south end is confirmed. The FVRD operates a sewer system for Cultus Lake in Electoral Area H and publishes a service area map; lots outside a sewer service area use private septic systems regulated by the Fraser Health Authority.

Governing zoning and plans (FVRD / Park Board — never Chilliwack's bylaws): FVRD Cultus Lake Park Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016 zones the Park lease lands. PlanCultus, Cultus Lake Park Plan Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, covers the Park including the east-side lots; the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115, covers Area H land outside the Park.

Most of the "east shore" is a provincial park, not a housing market. Cultus Lake Provincial Park occupies most of the east shore; the private housing is the Park lease-lot strip on Lakeshore Drive/Munroe Avenue plus one manufactured-home park on the highway. A buyer searching "Cultus Lake East condos" is searching a sub-area with no condo stock at all.

The same park home was marketed as both 45+ and 55+ within one listing cycle. Home 28 at Cultus Lake Village was listed in spring 2026 as a "45+ age park" and later with the park described as a "55+ age park", in otherwise near-identical text. A 45+ label could never be a valid BC strata bylaw — but this is a manufactured-home park, where the age rule is the park's own under tenancy regulation, so only the park's written rules settle it.

Sewer at the lake is an area-by-area build-out. The FVRD operates a sewer system for Cultus Lake in Electoral Area H and publishes a Cultus Lake Service Area Map; lots outside a sewer service area use private septic systems regulated by the Fraser Health Authority — connection status is a per-lot check on the east shore too.

A Chilliwack mailing address does not make this Chilliwack. Governance, zoning, plans and taxes here run through the Cultus Lake Park Board and the FVRD (Electoral Area H) — Park Plan Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, Park Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016, and the rural tax regime — not through the City of Chilliwack.

parts.t: The province-wide rules are on one page:
BC condo buying rules

items.t: The north end's only condominium markets itself on scarcity, not age. Lakeside's own site states only 5 of its 21 homes remain, with a private dock and a boat slip for each home — a recreational product aimed at weekend and second-home buyers, with no age restriction anywhere in its material. Do not let a "Cultus Lake condos" search imply a condo market here: it is one 21-home building.

The Park is self-funded, which is why the lease charges matter. Park Board community material records that Cultus Lake Park receives no local, provincial or federal funding and is entirely self-sustaining, with more than 1,500 residential leaseholders — lease charges are the Park's operating revenue, not a tax bill by another name. That frame does not apply to Lakeside's freehold parcel, which is why the tenure check comes first.

The lake's sewage servicing is being rebuilt in stages, north side first. The FVRD's North Cultus wastewater treatment plant was commissioned in April 2025 under the FVRD Liquid Waste Management Plan (approved 2019), for Class A effluent plus phosphorus removal — 2025 was its first operational year, and it serves the lake's north side. Whether a specific north-end lot is connected is a per-lot check.

"Cultus Lake North" is an emergency-planning name as much as a real estate one. The FVRD uses "Cultus Lake North" as a community location name in its Area H Evacuation Guide; it is not a municipal neighbourhood name, and no official MLS boundary for it is published by the Park Board or the FVRD.

The Village Centre is a negotiation, not a presale. Village Centre redevelopment is a Park Board request-for-proposals process with a preferred proponent in negotiations. A buyer told a new condo project is "coming" at the Village Centre is being told about an RFP — no developer, no disclosure statement, no units.
BC condo buying rules

Taxes (rural regime, not Chilliwack's dates): Electoral Area H properties pay FVRD and provincial rural taxes plus service-area levies. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11, rural taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid after July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid after October 31. Chilliwack's penalty dates do not apply to Cultus Lake. Service detail: the South Cultus Lake sewer service area was established by Bylaw No. 1416, 2017, with a parcel tax under Bylaw No. 1497, 2018; Amendment Bylaw No. 1779, 2025 set the per-parcel amount as the annual requisition divided equally by parcels on the roll. The FVRD's Area H residential rates list Water – Cultus Lake and Sewer – Cultus Lake South as "No Utility Billing / Property Taxes: Yes" (tax-funded); confirm the specific lot is a participant. Source: Area H - Residential Rates 2026.pdf

The south end's sewer tax is shared equally, not metered. Amendment Bylaw No. 1779, 2025 set the South Cultus Lake sewer parcel tax as the annual requisition divided equally by the parcels on the roll — every participating parcel pays the same amount regardless of use, and the FVRD's Area H rates show the south sewer and the Cultus Lake water service as tax-funded with no separate utility bill (the north sewer, by contrast, carries a flat rate plus taxes). Area H - Residential Rates 2026.pdf

"Bare land strata" is the whole story at Lindell Beach. All three named communities sell a detached house or cottage, but the title is a bare land strata lot: strata fees, bylaws, a depreciation report and a CRF stand behind the cottage, and the Form B — not the cottage's appearance — is where a buyer learns what the strata maintains and what the lot owner does.

The local hazards are creek fans, not the Fraser River. The governing local hazards at Lindell Beach are lake-level and creek (Frosst Creek) debris/flood events on the Cultus Lake alluvial fans; the FVRD funds sediment-basin cleanouts at Frosst Creek and Elbow Creek in this area, and its Area H guide lists flooding, landslide and slope stability, interface fire, debris slides and flash flooding.
There are no SnapStats numbers for anywhere at Cultus Lake. Lindell Beach is a CADREB board sub-area under the Cultus Lake MLS area, not an FVREB reporting row.

Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) is at the south end of the lake. The PlanCultus plan map shows Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) at the south end — a neighbouring jurisdiction a south-end buyer will see on maps and in addressing, distinct from both the Park and the FVRD lots.

The Holiday Resort's tenure is documented by a court, not a brochure. The only hard source on the Lindell Beach Holiday Resort's model is the BC Court of Appeal's 2009 record (owned pre-fabricated trailer on a leased pad; 130 sites, 100 occupied at that time) — the resort itself publishes no current lease terms.

Aquadel Crossing answers to two civic numbers in public sources. The developer address is 1885 Columbia Valley Rd while a current listing records the community at 1880 Columbia Valley Road — a small conflict that matters for title searches, locator runs and showing directions, and one to settle from the strata plan rather than from either marketing source.
BC condo buying rules

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Cultus Lake
Where the townhomes are and what to know

items.t: Governance: the east shore of Cultus Lake is Cultus Lake Provincial Park, Cultus Lake Park lease lots, and FVRD Electoral Area H land south of the City of Chilliwack. "Cultus Lake East" is not an official municipal neighbourhood name; the east-side residential lots sit inside Cultus Lake Park, governed by the Cultus Lake Park Board.
Nearby areas: Cultus Lake North (same lake), Cultus Lake South / Lindell Beach, Columbia Valley to the southeast, Sardis (Chilliwack) to the north.

Where housing sits: most of the east shore is Cultus Lake Provincial Park (Entrance Bay, Clear Creek, Delta Grove and Maple Bay campgrounds; Entrance Bay and Maple Bay day-use areas with wharfs and sandy beaches; trails including Teapot Hill, Seven Sisters, Giant Douglas-fir, Maple Bay and the Cultus Lake Horse Trail).
Schools: the only school located at the lake is Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School (K–5) at the north end — the Ministry-listed name in that form. Graham Secondary School.

Transit and roads: BC Transit route 56 Cultus Lake runs along Columbia Valley Highway on the east-shore side between Chilliwack (Cottonwood Mall / Promontory area) and the Cultus Lake Marina stop; service is seasonal, summer only, with no year-round transit service to the Cultus Lake community. Columbia Valley Highway is the east-shore road; BC Parks states the park entrance is 10 km from the Sardis exit of Highway 1 via Columbia Valley Highway, and the park is 11 km southwest of Chilliwack with access off Highway 1 at the Yarrow or Sardis exits.

Hazards: BC Parks states the Cultus Lake Horse Trail along the east side crosses an active landslide area, with warning signage, and advises visitors not to cross during intense rainfall; BC Parks also notes steep, dangerous drop-offs along the lakeshore and a sudden change in water depth close to shore. The FVRD provides a Flood and Debris Control service in Electoral Area H.

Governance: the north end of Cultus Lake is largely Cultus Lake Park, governed by the Cultus Lake Park Board, inside Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area H, south of the City of Chilliwack. "Cultus Lake North" is used by the FVRD as a community location name in its Area H Evacuation Guide; it is not a municipal neighbourhood name. The Park operates under the Cultus Lake Park Act.
Nearby areas: Cultus Lake East and Cultus Lake South (same lake), Columbia Valley to the south, Sardis and Yarrow (Chilliwack) to the north.

Where housing sits: single-detached homes and cabins on Park Board leased lots along Sunnyside Boulevard and the Park's residential streets, many held as recreational/second homes, plus the one condominium at 3175 Columbia Valley Highway. Main Beach is the Park Board's main public beach at the north end; Sunnyside Campground, 4165 Columbia Valley Highway, is 65 acres with seasonal, full hook-up and tenting sites, a boat launch and playgrounds; Cultus Lake Community Hall is at 4220 Columbia Valley Highway.

Schools: the only public school at the lake is Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School, K to Grade 5, at 71 Sunnyside Blvd — the Ministry-listed name in that form. Graham Secondary), and G.W. Graham Secondary.

Transit and roads: BC Transit route 56 Cultus Lake runs between Chilliwack (Cottonwood Mall / Promontory area) and the Cultus Lake Marina stop via Vedder Road and Columbia Valley Highway; service is seasonal — summer months only, with no year-round transit service to Cultus Lake Park. Columbia Valley Highway is the access road at the north end and Sunnyside Boulevard leads into the Park; Highway 1 is reached via the Sardis or Yarrow exits.

Shopping: the Village Centre / commercial plaza at Columbia Valley Highway and Sunnyside Boulevard is the Park commercial area designated in PlanCultus; a Park Board Village Centre committee agenda names Cultus Lake Superette as the grocery and convenience store at the plaza, without a street address. No Fraser Valley Regional Library branch is at Cultus Lake; the nearest is Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road, Chilliwack.

Hazards: the FVRD Evacuation Guide for Area H lists flooding, landslide and slope stability, interface fire, debris slides and flash flooding among local hazards, and the FVRD provides a Flood and Debris Control service in Area H.
Health: Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Rd, Chilliwack, and the Chilliwack Urgent and Primary Care Centre, #104 - 7955 Evans Road, Chilliwack (Fraser Health).

Boundaries: no official MLS boundary for Cultus Lake South is published by the FVRD or the Park Board. Nearby areas: Cultus Lake North and Cultus Lake East (same lake), Columbia Valley to the southeast, Yarrow and Sardis (Chilliwack) to the north. Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) is shown on the PlanCultus plan map at the south end of the lake.

A fresh townhouse search for this area returns other shores' stock. The November 2, 2026 verification search for Cultus Lake townhouse complexes surfaced Lakeside units (North), Aquadel Crossing homes (South, Lindell Beach) and short-term-rental cottages described as townhouses — none of it east-shore townhouse stock.

items.t: Two Cultus Lake "projects" in search results are not stock. The Village Centre redevelopment is a Park Board RFP process with a preferred proponent in negotiations — no building is named and nothing can be bought — and the 3636 Columbia Valley Road listing is vacant land for an unbuilt 6-lot subdivision. Neither is a presale a buyer can write on today.

There are no SnapStats numbers for anywhere at Cultus Lake. The SnapStats FVR September 2026 report contains no Chilliwack section at all, and neither does the GVR report; CADREB publishes no area stats — any inventory, sales-ratio or median figure quoted for this sub-area has no source in the named stats programs.

There are no stats for anywhere at Cultus Lake in the named programs. The SnapStats FVR and GVR September 2026 reports contain no Chilliwack section at all, and CADREB publishes no area stats. Lindell Beach is a CADREB board sub-area under the Cultus Lake MLS area.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Cultus Lake
What trades here

items.t: Homes inside Cultus Lake Park sit on leased lots administered by the Cultus Lake Park Board — leasehold, not freehold — and the Park operates under the Cultus Lake Park Act. A buyer purchases the home and the leasehold interest, not freehold land and not a strata lot.

East-shore lease lots — the shore's own land form: single-detached homes and cabins on waterfront (R-3) and hillside (R-4) lease lots along Lakeshore Drive and Munroe Avenue; manufactured homes are also a permitted primary use in R-3. In R-3 the permitted primary uses are a single-detached dwelling or a manufactured home, one dwelling per lot, for lots fronting on Cultus Lake; Amendment Bylaw No. 1672 added R-5 Lower Lakeshore Drive and R-6 Upper Lakeshore Drive zones and amended R-4 height.
The lake's one freehold exception, Lakeside at Cultus Lake, is north-end built condo stock, cross-referenced below, not east-shore land.

PAD-TENURE RECORD only — Cultus Lake Village MHP, 3942 Columbia Valley Road: A manufactured home on a rented pad is not lot stock and not land ownership — the buyer owns the manufactured home and rents the pad.

Cottonwood Village, a pad-rental manufactured-home park whose board placement conflicts (West Chilliwack vs Sardis West Vedder) — the conflict stays unresolved, it is assigned nowhere, and it is a pad-rental park in any case.

blocks.text: Where lots come up and what to know

items.t: The SnapStats FVR September 2026 report contains no Chilliwack section at all and the GVR report has none either; CADREB publishes no area stats.

Parks and recreation: Cultus Lake Provincial Park occupies most of the east shore, with Entrance Bay, Clear Creek, Delta Grove and Maple Bay campgrounds, Entrance Bay and Maple Bay day-use areas with wharfs and sandy beaches, and trails including Teapot Hill, Seven Sisters, Giant Douglas-fir, Maple Bay and the Cultus Lake Horse Trail.

Schools (SD33 Chilliwack, Ministry-listed names): SD33 catchments are address-based, but no catchment is confirmed for the east shore. The only school located at the lake is Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School (K–5) at the north end. Graham Secondary School.
How people search for it: "Cultus Lake East," "Lakeshore Drive" and "Munroe Avenue" (the east-shore lease-lot streets named in the Park zoning bylaw).
Graham Secondary), and G.W. Graham Secondary. That result is for that address only and is non-transferable.

Parks, shopping and civic anchors: Main Beach is the Park Board's main public beach at the north end; Sunnyside Campground, 4165 Columbia Valley Highway, is 65 acres with seasonal, full hook-up and tenting sites, a boat launch and playgrounds; Cultus Lake Community Hall is at 4220 Columbia Valley Highway. The Village Centre / commercial plaza at Columbia Valley Highway and Sunnyside Boulevard is the Park commercial area designated in PlanCultus; a Park Board Village Centre committee agenda names Cultus Lake Superette as the grocery and convenience store at the plaza, without a street address. No Fraser Valley Regional Library branch is at Cultus Lake; nearest is Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road, Chilliwack.
How people search for it: "Cultus Lake North," "Cultus Lake," "Sunnyside" (the Park's west-side campground/residential road area).

The south end of Cultus Lake, including Lindell Beach on the south shore, is in Fraser Valley Regional District (FVRD) Electoral Area H, south of the City of Chilliwack, and outside the Cultus Lake Park Board lease lands; the FVRD lists Lindell Beach, Columbia Valley and Cultus Lake as the communities of Electoral Area H.

Nearby areas: Cultus Lake North and Cultus Lake East (same lake), Columbia Valley to the southeast, and Yarrow and Sardis (Chilliwack) to the north. Columbia Valley Road/Highway serves the populated area around the lake and provides one-way-in, one-way-out access, north to the Sardis and Yarrow exits of Highway 1.

Land shape: single-detached homes and recreational cottages around Lindell Beach and the south shore, outside the Park lease system; much of the non-mountainous part of Electoral Area H west of Lindell Beach is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, and the FVRD Evacuation Guide for Area H lists flooding, landslide and slope stability, interface fire, debris slides and flash flooding among local hazards. Housing Needs Report.pdf

Schools (SD33 Chilliwack, Ministry-listed names): no public school is located at the south end; the only school at the lake is Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School (K to Grade 5) at the north end. SD33 catchments are address-based and no sample south-end address was run in a locator for this sub-area.

Transit: BC Transit route 56 Cultus Lake runs between Chilliwack (Cottonwood Mall / Promontory) and the Cultus Lake Marina stop at the north end via Vedder Road and Columbia Valley Highway; the route does not extend to Lindell Beach or the south end, and service to the lake is seasonal in summer only.

Shopping and health: no shopping centre or grocery store at the south end is confirmed. Chilliwack General Hospital is at 45600 Menholm Rd, Chilliwack; the nearest library branch is Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road, Chilliwack.

Plans — Cultus Lake Park / FVRD Electoral Area H (never Chilliwack): PlanCultus, Cultus Lake Park Plan Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, covers Cultus Lake Park including the east-side residential lots and designates them Residential; the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115, covers Area H land outside the Park. Chilliwack's OCP 5500, SSMUH 5395 and Zoning 5000 belong to the City of Chilliwack only and are never imported here.

Hazards: BC Parks documents an active landslide area on the east-side Horse Trail and steep lakeshore drop-offs with a sudden change in water depth close to shore — get a geotechnical read on hillside lots. The FVRD provides a Flood and Debris Control service in Electoral Area H.
The mailing address lies about the jurisdiction (Nov 1, 2026).
The lake's bare-land strata is at the other end of the lake (Nov 1, 2026).
The east shore's grocery run is to Sardis (Nov 1, 2026). Most of the east shore is provincial park land with no grocery on it.
One home, two age rules, same year (2026). Cultus Lake Village home No. 28 was listed as a "45+ age park" in spring 2026 and as a "55+ age park" later in near-identical text.

items.t: The campground is part of the housing picture's edge (Nov 1, 2026). Sunnyside Campground (4165 Columbia Valley Highway) is a 65-acre Park Board campground with seasonal, full hook-up and tenting sites, a boat launch and playgrounds — seasonal neighbours for the Sunnyside lease lots, and not housing stock of any kind.

The Village Centre grocery has no official street address (Nov 1, 2026). A Park Board committee agenda names Cultus Lake Superette as the grocery and convenience store at the Village Centre plaza (Columbia Valley Highway at Sunnyside Boulevard) without a street address.
A school locator note follows the middle schoolers out (Nov 1, 2026). Graham Secondary — the secondary path is stated in the locator itself, for that address only.
BC land buying rules

The south shore is the freehold shore (Nov 1, 2026). The defining fact of this area is the tenure contrast: north and east shore homes sit in the Cultus Lake Park leasehold system, while south-end homes are freehold or bare-land strata under FVRD bylaws — a buyer who imports the Park lease assumption will read the wrong documents entirely.

One road in, one road out (May 14, 2025). The FVRD's Area H update with emergency and evacuation plans records that Columbia Valley Road/Highway provides the populated area's only access, north to the Sardis and Yarrow exits of Highway 1 — the single-road reality drives emergency planning and summer traffic at the south end.

The year-round campground and the horse trail are at this end (Nov 1, 2026). Delta Grove Campground, in Cultus Lake Provincial Park at the southeast end of the lake, is the provincial park campground operating year-round, and the Watt Creek trailhead at the south end of the park is where the 20 km Cultus Lake Horse Trail from Edmeston Road ends.

Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) is shown at the south end (Nov 1, 2026). The PlanCultus plan map shows Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) at the south end of the lake — neighbouring jurisdiction a land buyer at the south shore should know exists on the plan map.

In the strata cottage communities (Creekside Mills, The Cottages and Aquadel Crossing), confirm what the strata owns versus what sits on the lot. The Province's strata buying guidance applies: review bylaws, rules, fees and any special levies.
BC land buying rules

blocks.text: Acreage and rural land in Cultus Lake

The Cultus Lake land form here is Park Board LEASE lots — east shore = R-3 waterfront / R-4 hillside lease lots inside Cultus Lake Park, plus provincial park land — so "land" on this shore means a leasehold interest, not a lot or acreage purchase.

The Cultus Lake land form here is Park Board LEASE lots — north shore = R-1/R-2 Sunnyside Blvd lease lots inside Cultus Lake Park — plus one freehold waterfront condo site (built stock, not land), so "land" on this shore means a leasehold interest, not a lot or acreage purchase.
The ground in Cultus Lake East

items.t: East-shore lease lots: single-detached homes and cabins on waterfront (R-3) and hillside (R-4) lease lots along Lakeshore Drive and Munroe Avenue; manufactured homes are also a permitted primary use in R-3. In R-3 the permitted primary uses are a single-detached dwelling or a manufactured home, one dwelling per lot, for lots fronting on Cultus Lake; Amendment Bylaw No. 1672 added R-5 Lower Lakeshore Drive and R-6 Upper Lakeshore Drive zones and amended R-4 height.
Fee-simple lots: The lake's one freehold exception, Lakeside at Cultus Lake, is north-end built condo stock, cross-referenced below, not east-shore land.
PAD-TENURE RECORD only: A manufactured home on a rented pad is not lot stock, not land ownership and not acreage — the buyer owns the manufactured home and rents the pad.

Cottonwood Village, a pad-rental manufactured-home park whose board placement conflicts (West Chilliwack vs Sardis West Vedder) — the conflict stays unresolved, it is assigned nowhere, and it is a pad-rental park in any case.
Serviced vs unserviced: Never price an east-shore lot as serviced fee-simple ground on a listing's say-so.

blocks.text: The ground in Cultus Lake North

items.t: North-end lease lots: single-detached homes and cabins on leased lots inside Cultus Lake Park, many held as recreational/second homes, on Sunnyside Boulevard and the Park's residential streets.

North-end zones: the FVRD's Cultus Lake Park Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016 zones the Park lease lands; zones in this area include R-1 Suburban Residential (one single-detached dwelling per lot) and R-2 Urban Residential (one single-detached dwelling plus one secondary suite). The bylaw tables state no minimum lot area figure for R-1/R-2.
Fee-simple lots: a fee-simple lot carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees.
Serviced vs unserviced: Never price a north-end lot as serviced fee-simple ground on a listing's say-so.

blocks.text: The ground in Cultus Lake South

items.t: Fee-simple parcels: Unlike the north and east shores, south-end homes are outside the Cultus Lake Park leasehold system — land use is under the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115, and PlanCultus (Bylaw No. 1080, 2016) applies only inside Cultus Lake Park at the north end. Under the OCP designations the only residential use permitted is single family residential use, with housing needs met mainly through infill in existing hamlets. A fee-simple parcel carries no strata corporation, no Form B and no strata fees. Housing Needs Report.pdf

Serviced vs unserviced: the FVRD operates a sewer system for Cultus Lake in Electoral Area H and publishes a Cultus Lake Service Area Map; lots outside a sewer service area use private septic systems regulated by the Fraser Health Authority. Whether any given parcel is inside the service area is a per-lot check against that map — never price a south-shore parcel as serviced ground on a listing's say-so.
Hobby vs working-farm ground: On ALR parcels west of Lindell Beach the governing frame is farm use under the ALC rules.

blocks.text: Where the acreages are and what to know

items.t: Schools are address-based in SD33. The one settled locator chain for this sub-area is Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School → Mount Slesse Middle → G.W. Graham Secondary. Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School (K–5) at 71 Sunnyside Blvd is the only public school located at the lake.

Most of the east shore is a provincial park, not a subdivision (BC Parks, Nov 1, 2026): Cultus Lake Provincial Park occupies most of the east shore, with four campgrounds (Entrance Bay, Clear Creek, Delta Grove, Maple Bay) and day-use areas at Entrance Bay and Maple Bay — the lease lots sit inside a park landscape, which is why there is no fee-simple lot market to discover.

The landslide is signed, not rumoured (BC Parks, Nov 1, 2026): The Cultus Lake Horse Trail along the east side crosses an active landslide area with warning signage, and BC Parks advises visitors not to cross during intense rainfall — the geotechnical diligence in starts from an official warning, not local lore.
One home, two age rules, no answer (MLS record, Nov 1, 2026): Village MHP home No. 28 was listed "45+" in spring 2026 and "55+" later in otherwise near-identical text.

parts.t: The province-wide rules are on one page:
BC acreage buying rules

items.t: The Park is 640 acres at the north end (Park Board, Nov 1, 2026): Cultus Lake Park covers 640 acres at the north end of the lake, with the Village Centre site immediately south of Columbia Valley Highway at Sunnyside Boulevard — the lease lots, Main Beach and the commercial plaza all sit inside one Park Board jurisdiction, which is why no municipal bylaw or city stat describes this area.

The hazard list is an evacuation guide, not a brochure (FVRD, Nov 1, 2026): Flooding, landslide and slope stability, interface fire, debris slides and flash flooding are listed in the FVRD's Area H Evacuation Guide itself — the document a north-end owner should actually keep, and the reason insurance diligence here starts with hazards, not amenities.
BC acreage buying rules

The lake has two opposite tenure systems: The north end is Park Board leasehold under PlanCultus (Bylaw No. 1080, 2016); the south end is fee-simple and bare land strata under the FVRD OCP for Electoral Areas E and H (Bylaw No. 1115). A buyer who prices a south-shore parcel with a leasehold discount — or a north-end lease lot as freehold — has the lake backwards.

One road in, one road out: Columbia Valley Road is the only access, and the FVRD's own Area H evacuation material lists flooding, landslide and slope stability, interface fire, debris slides and flash flooding among local hazards — the access and hazard facts belong in the price discussion for any larger parcel, not in the fine print.
BC acreage buying rules

blocks.text: Mobile and manufactured homes in Cultus Lake
The east shore otherwise has no fee-simple bare-land market: its residential lots are Park Board LEASE lots.
The parks and communities

items.t: Cultus Lake Village (Cultus Lake Village Manufactured Home Park): Board listing data records zoning "MHP", non-strata tenure, an MLS legal description naming the "Cultus Lake Village Manufactured Home Park", and bylaw restrictions including "Age Restrictions"; listings describe it as "family-owned and operated park for over 25 years". TENURE LINE: a home in this park sits on a rented pad — the buyer owns the home as a chattel and rents the pad; there is no strata lot, no Park Board lease and no land ownership.

East-shore Park Board lease lots: Homes inside Cultus Lake Park sit on leased lots under the Cultus Lake Park Board — leasehold, not freehold. FVRD Cultus Lake Park Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016 sets the zones for the Park lease lands: in R-3, the permitted primary uses are a single-detached dwelling or a manufactured home, one dwelling per lot, for lots fronting on Cultus Lake; Amendment Bylaw No. 1672 added R-5 Lower Lakeshore Drive and R-6 Upper Lakeshore Drive zones and amended R-4 height. PlanCultus, Cultus Lake Park Plan Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, covers the Park including the east-side residential lots; the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115, covers Area H land outside the Park.

blocks.text: Mobile home parks and what to know

items.t: Where it sits: the Cultus Lake Park Plan, Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, designates the residential lots on the east side of the lake and the Mountainview Road and Park Drive areas as Residential, and BC Parks states Columbia Valley Highway bisects the southeast section of Cultus Lake Provincial Park. The east-shore lease-lot streets named in the Park zoning bylaw are Lakeshore Drive and Munroe Avenue. Nearby areas: Cultus Lake North (same lake), Cultus Lake South / Lindell Beach, Columbia Valley to the southeast, Sardis (Chilliwack) to the north.

Taxes: Electoral Area H properties pay FVRD and provincial rural taxes plus service-area levies; under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, rural taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid on October 31.

This ground is not Chilliwack, whatever the mailing address says: The east shore is FVRD Electoral Area H and Cultus Lake Park Board land. A buyer reading a "Chilliwack" page for an east-shore lot is reading the wrong municipality's rules.

R-3 is the one east-shore zone that names a manufactured home as a primary use: On the waterfront lease lots, the zoning bylaw permits one single-detached dwelling or one manufactured home per lot — so a "manufactured home on the east shore" is most often a leasehold home on Park land, not a pad in a park and not a fee-simple purchase. R-5/R-6 now apply on Lower and Upper Lakeshore Drive after Amendment Bylaw No. 1672.

The east shore has documented slope and shoreline hazards: BC Parks documents an active landslide area on the east-side Horse Trail (with signage, and advice not to cross during intense rainfall) and steep lakeshore drop-offs with a sudden change in water depth close to shore — get a geotechnical read on hillside (R-4/R-6) lots.

parts.t: The province-wide rules are on one page:
BC mobile home buying rules

items.t: The hazard list here is longer than a buyer's first read: The FVRD Area H Evacuation Guide lists flooding, landslide and slope stability, interface fire, debris slides and flash flooding among local hazards — read it and price insurance accordingly before writing on a north-end home.

Year-round living here means driving: Route 56 runs in summer only, the Village Centre is the Park's only commercial area, and the Village Centre redevelopment is a Park Board RFP process with a preferred proponent in negotiations — not a presale a buyer can price.
BC mobile home buying rules

The mailing address lies about the government: South-shore properties carry Chilliwack-area addresses, but the governing bodies are the FVRD (Electoral Area H) and, for rural taxes, the Province — Chilliwack bylaws, tax penalties and servicing standards do not apply here.

Aquadel Crossing answers to two civic numbers in public sources: — 1885 Columbia Valley Rd (developer) vs 1880 Columbia Valley Road (a current listing) — a small conflict that matters for title searches and showing directions; settle it from the strata plan.

There is no bus to Lindell Beach, and one road in and out: Route 56 ends at the north-end marina and is summer-only, and Columbia Valley Road is the single access — both facts shape year-round living, emergency planning and summer traffic on the south shore.

What a duplex looks like in Cultus Lake South

items.t: The usual duplex form: Single-detached homes and recreational cottages around Lindell Beach and the south shore, outside the Park lease system, on fee-simple lots plus the bare-land strata cottage communities below. Under the FVRD OCP for Electoral Areas E and H, the only residential use permitted under the plan designations is single family residential use, with housing needs met mainly through infill in existing hamlets — the plan form itself is a single-family form, not a two-unit duplex form.

items.t: Leases, zoning, sewer and taxes at the lake:
buying a home at Cultus Lake: the rules

faq.a: Homes inside Cultus Lake Park are on leased lots under the Cultus Lake Park Board, under FVRD Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016 (R-3/R-4 on this shore). Cultus Lake Village is different again: a privately owned manufactured-home park — a pad tenancy, not a Park Board lease and not freehold land.
faq.q: Is housing on the east shore freehold or leasehold?

faq.a: Listings for the same park in the same year state both "45+" and "55+" — including the same home listed both ways. Get the park's written rule and assignment-consent position before writing.
faq.q: Is Cultus Lake Village a 55+ park?

faq.a: The home, on a rented pad under the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act. Pad-rent increases are capped (2026: 2.3% plus a proportional amount; 2027: 2.2% plus proportional), and the park can refuse an assignment to a purchaser who does not meet its age requirement where its sites are age-reserved. The current pad rent for a specific site: confirm with the park — listing-stated figures are per-home and dated.
faq.q: What does a manufactured home in the park actually give me?

faq.a: For Park lease lots, the lease and Park bylaws govern — read them before assuming any rental use; the strata rental-void rule does not apply because there is no strata. For a park home, the tenancy agreement and park rules govern.
faq.q: Can I rent out an east-shore home?

faq.a: One building: Lakeside at Cultus Lake, 3175 Columbia Valley Highway — 21 condominium homes on freehold waterfront land (developer source), built 2019 per listing data, each with a boat slip per the developer and the building's site. Everything else at the north end is a Park Board leasehold home or cabin.
faq.q: What condos can I buy at the north end of Cultus Lake?

faq.a: No — that is its defining difference. The developer describes freehold waterfront land, while homes inside Cultus Lake Park sit on leased lots administered by the Park Board under the Cultus Lake Park Act. Confirm the strata plan and title on the Form B and disclosure documents for the specific unit.
faq.q: Is Lakeside leasehold like the rest of the Park?

faq.a: It is a general-market recreational condominium.
faq.q: Is Lakeside a 55+ building?

faq.a: There is no fee-simple bare-land market on the east shore; the residential land form is Park Board LEASE lots (R-3 waterfront / R-4 hillside) inside Cultus Lake Park, plus provincial park land. What a buyer purchases is the home and the leasehold interest.
faq.q: Can I actually buy an acreage on the east shore of Cultus Lake?

faq.a: The home plus the leasehold interest under the Cultus Lake Park Board, under the Cultus Lake Park Act and PlanCultus (Bylaw No. 1080, 2016). Park lease lots pay Park Board lease charges rather than a standard municipal tax bill.
faq.q: What exactly does a lease-lot purchase include — and what does it cost to hold?

faq.a: Under FVRD Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016, R-3 Waterfront Residential permits one single-detached dwelling or one manufactured home per waterfront lot; R-5/R-6 now apply on Lower and Upper Lakeshore Drive after Amendment Bylaw No. 1672, which also amended R-4 height.
faq.q: What can I build or keep on an R-3 or R-4 lot?

faq.a: The RURAL regime — Taxation (Rural Area) Act s.11: a 5% penalty after Jul 2 and a further 5% after Oct 31 — not any City of Chilliwack schedule. Park lots themselves pay Park Board lease charges instead of a municipal tax bill.
faq.q: Which taxes and penalties apply if I own Area H land outside the Park?

faq.a: There is no fee-simple bare-land market on the north shore; the residential land form is Park Board LEASE lots (R-1/R-2, Sunnyside Blvd) inside Cultus Lake Park, plus one freehold condo site that is built stock. What a lease-lot buyer purchases is the home and the leasehold interest.
faq.q: Can I actually buy an acreage at the north end of Cultus Lake?

faq.a: The lease itself and the Park bylaws: homes in Cultus Lake Park are on Park Board leased lots under the Cultus Lake Park Act and PlanCultus (Bylaw No. 1080, 2016), paying Park Board lease charges rather than a municipal tax bill.
faq.q: Start with the lease — what should I read first?

faq.a: No: you own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the MHPTA.
faq.q: If I buy in Cultus Lake Village, do I own the land?

faq.a: Confirm financing for the specific home and its tenure before removing subjects.
faq.q: Can I get a mortgage on a park home or a Park lease-lot home?

faq.a: No — homes inside the Park sit on leased lots administered by the Cultus Lake Park Board: you purchase the home and the leasehold interest, not freehold land and not a strata lot. That is also different from a pad tenancy: the north-shore lease runs on the Park Board lease and Park bylaws, not the MHPTA pad block.
faq.q: If I buy a home inside Cultus Lake Park, do I own the land?

faq.a: No: you own the home (a chattel) and rent the pad — the park owns the land, and your right to the site is the assigned pad tenancy under the MHPTA.
faq.q: If I buy in a pad-rental park elsewhere at the lake, do I own the land?

faq.a: Confirm financing for the specific home and its tenure before removing subjects.
faq.q: Can I get a mortgage on a park home or a Park lease-lot home?

faq.a: There is no known duplex at the south end to buy a side of. What sells here is a whole fee-simple home/cottage, or a whole bare-land strata lot with its cottage in one of the three named communities.
faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex at the south end?

faq.a: The south end is not Park Board leasehold: Tenure here is freehold or bare land strata under FVRD bylaws, so title and strata documents, not a Park lease, drive the deal.
faq.q: Is the south end leasehold like the north end?

faq.a: No. It is FVRD Electoral Area H, south of the City of Chilliwack and outside the Cultus Lake Park Board boundary. Chilliwack bylaws and tax dates do not apply.
faq.q: Is Cultus Lake South part of Chilliwack?

faq.a: Confirm for the exact lot: The FVRD sewer service covers a mapped service area, and lots outside it rely on private septic systems regulated by Fraser Health.
faq.q: Sewer or septic?
